title: Light-touch handshake + tool-call debugger PRD (draft)
summary: Short PRD draft proposing a lightweight client-server handshake for streaming tool-calls plus a companion developer-facing "debugger" surface in the SDK and Console. Goal: make tool integrations reliable and debuggable with minimal protocol overhead and without requiring heavy developer instrumentation.
goals: 1) Reduce flakiness and developer time-to-inspect for tool-calls over streaming. 2) Keep handshake payloads compact to preserve latency and token cost. 3) Provide clear, actionable debug signals surfaced in SDK and Console without additional instrumentation from customer. 4) Maintain compatibility with existing incremental/partial-response surfaces.
non_goals: 1) Replacing all existing hosted-api streaming contracts — this is additive and opt-in. 2) Full visual UI rewrite for Console; Console surface is minimal (logs + annotated frames). 3) Implementing a custom protocol for on-prem/private deployments in this phase (may be considered later).
background_and_problem_statement: Teams building tool-enabled UIs frequently run into ambiguous failures: tool responses arrive but are malformed, or tool calls silently time out and app-level retries spike costs. Current hosted streaming surface provides partial frames and typed-tool envelopes but lacks a low-cost, standardized way to: (a) confirm tool eligibility/contract at low latency, (b) attach compact diagnostic context to failing tool-calls, and (c) provide developers an SDK-first 'replayable' inspection flow. The result: long debug cycles, increased support tickets, and workarounds that add latency or duplicate logic in customer code.
proposal_overview:
Introduce a "light-touch handshake" pattern plus an SDK Debugger object.

Light-touch handshake: a tiny pre-call exchange (O(100) bytes) that confirms tool availability, preferred serialization, and quick validation checks (schema hash, auth hint). This handshake is optional and only used for tool-calls flagged with 'dbg=on' or when SDK detects repeated failures.

SDK Debugger: a developer-visible runtime component that captures the handshake, frame-level events, canonicalized request/response snippets, and an immutable trace id. It exposes a replay helper (local only) that can re-synthesize the exact minimal call payloads and annotate Console logs with likely root causes.
requirements: Protocol: pre-call handshake <= 1 round-trip or piggybacked on an initial small frame when using streaming sockets
Handshake payloads must be compact (prefer <256 bytes serialized) and extensible (key-value small map)
SDK should default handshake off; enable via per-call flag, env var, or automatic heuristics after N failures

Debugger must capture: trace_id, timestamps (handshake start/end, first-byte, last-byte), serialized compact request, tool id/version, server-side rejection code (if any), and optional model/route used
Console should surface searchable debug traces and allow limited (read-only) replay of request text and a side-by-side view of frames
Tool providers cannot opt-out of reporting minimal diagnostic verdicts (e.g., schema-mismatch, auth-failure) — these are surfaced as enumerated short codes to prevent PII leakage
Must integrate with existing streaming partial-response contracts and not break clients that ignore handshake frames
Telemetry: emit metrics per call (handshake latency, handshake_success:boolean, tool_error_code), exponential backoff if handshake increases observed latencies for callers
Security: handshake diagnostics must not include raw customer PII; SDK should scrub long contexts and attachments before storing trace data in Console logs
api_and_sdk_ergonomics_notes:
High-level SDK ergonomics:

- Minimal Opt-in: API surface should be 1 new optional param on tool invocation: { debug: boolean | 'auto' }. Default false.
- Transparent: When debug is true, SDK attaches a compact header/first-frame with handshake map and a generated trace_id.
- Replay Helper: SDK exposes debugger.replay(trace_id) that prints a sanitized CLI-friendly payload; no network calls unless explicitly requested with 'replay.send()'.
- CLI dev flow: local SDK should store traces under ~/.redwood/debugger/<trace_id>.json.gz (sanitized), enabling offline debugging and sharing with SRE/solutions teams without exposing full user data.

Example ergonomic goals for the developer:
- Enable with single flag when invoking SDK from local tests.
- See immediate reason codes and minimal context in Console within seconds after failure.
- No changes needed to server-side model routing or tool provider APIs beyond returning an enumerated short code when rejecting calls.
handshake_schema_and_example:
Light handshake map (example fields):
- trace_id: short uuid (base62)  
- tool_id: canonical tool identifier (string)  
- tool_schema_hash: hex8 (optional)  
- accept_serialization: [json, jsonl, compact-json]  
- client_hint_version: sdk semver  
- intent_hint: short tokenized verb (e.g. 'run-command', 'fetch-contacts')

Serialized form should be the smallest representation possible (binary protobuf or compact json). Example (compact JSON): {"t":"x9J3c","i":"run-command","u":"tool:cron-1","s":"a3f21b7c"}
error_modes_and_short_codes:
Enumerated short codes (server/tool provider responsibility) — each code is 2–3 chars max to keep frames tiny. Examples:
- OK  = success
- NA  = tool not available (capacity / region)
- SC  = schema mismatch
- AU  = auth failure
- TO  = tool timeout
- EX  = tool exception (generic)

SDK/Console mappings should translate codes to friendly suggestions (eg SC -> 'schema hash mismatch: check tool contract/version or re-deploy tool with compatible schema').
telemetry_metrics_and_alerting:
Emit the following metrics to our observability backend:
- hosted.tool.handshake.count (labels: tool_id, route, success)
- hosted.tool.handshake.latency_ms (p95/p50/p99)
- hosted.tool.call.error_codes (count by code)
- hosted.tool.debugger.replay_count (indicator of dev friction)

Alerting:
- Increase in NA/TO/SC codes > 3x baseline for a tool in 30m window -> Pager to oncall and alert owner
- Handshake latency > 200ms p95 for production routes -> SRE investigation runbook
console_surface_proposal:
Console additions (MVP):
- Debug traces list view: timestamp, trace_id, tool_id, short verdict code, route, search by trace_id
- Trace detail: compact timeline (handshake start, first-byte-of-response, error code), sanitized request snippet, server attempt id, model used, SDK version
- Replay button: 'Generate local payload' (does not send network call) and 'Request replay link' (generates ephemeral, time-limited link that SRE can use to run a reproducible test in a staging tenant)
- Privacy guard: all request snippets redacted by default; an account-level setting 'allow_debug_snippet_sharing' must be enabled to include limited snippets in support tickets
rollout_plan_and_phase_milestones:
Phase 0 (experimental) - SDK-only feature behind flag; handshake optional; no Console storage; local trace files only. Duration: 4 weeks.
Phase 1 - Console ingestion of sanitized traces for debug-enabled calls; expose trace listing and detail. Pilot with 5 internal+external partners. Duration: 6 weeks.
Phase 2 - Auto heuristics (sdk auto-on after repeated failures), server-side summarized metrics and alerting, replay link generation. Duration: 8 weeks.
Phase 3 - Evaluate expanding to Dedicated/Private runtimes and adding richer per-frame diffs. Duration: TBD.

Rollback: disable handshake by default via runtime flag; preserve existing streaming semantics for non-handshake calls.
security_and_privacy_considerations:
- Never store full request/response raw blobs in Console by default.
- Apply deterministic scrubbing rules: remove long sequences (>512 chars) and strip email/phone patterns unless account-level permission is set.
- Trace IDs should be opaque and not guessable; expiration policy for Console traces (default retention 30 days for debug traces).
- For customers requiring no external debug storage (enterprise), SDK will offer an 'on-prem debug collector' mode where traces are written to customer-provided S3/KV and Console shows only pointers.
open_questions: Should handshake be a separate socket-level message or piggybacked as the first small streaming frame? Tradeoffs: additional RTT vs simpler parsing on servers.
What is the minimum set of short codes we can standardize across tool providers without adding friction to onboarding?
Is protobuf worth the added dependency in SDKs for compactness vs a tiny compact JSON line?
What privacy guard consent is reasonable for trial/pilot customers vs enterprise customers?
Replay link operational model: allow only in staging or permit production ephemeral replays?
